title: Characterizing the nitrogen-vacancy center singlet transition and its phonon sideband for absorption-based room-temperature magnetometry
authors: Tobias Probst, Florian Schall, Sebastian Heuft, Janina J. Schindler, Lukas Lindner, Sven Mägdefessel, Rüdiger Quay, Philipp Reineck, Alexander M. Zaitsev, Takeshi Ohshima, Matthias Weidemüller, Jan Jeske
abstract: Magnetometry with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond has shown great promise in recent years. In particular, absorption-based magnetometry techniques, employing a cavity to enhance the absorption length, can improve the contrast and sensitivity compared to conventional techniques based on reading out the NV$^-$ triplet fluorescence. The absorption techniques rely on magnetic-field-dependent absorption at the NV$^-$ singlet zero phonon line at 1042$\,$nm and its phonon sideband. In a cavity-enhanced spectroscopy approach, we study pump-laser- and microwave-induced cavity signal changes at room temperature over a spectral range of 680-1050$\,$nm. Through normalization, we eliminate the cavity-enhancement effect and provide quasi-single-pass values for the absorption and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The highest contrast is found at 1042$\,$nm, but multiple points of high contrast are found at the peaks of the phonon sideband. Additionally, cavity-enhanced ODMR contrasts in the range of 50-80$\,\%$ are presented. We further measure the broadband singlet absorption cross section at room temperature with a novel method through microwave-induced signal changes. This method is insensitive to pump-laser-induced signal changes by other defects and quantifies the room-temperature absorption strength of the singlet transition and its entire phonon sideband. We determine the absorption cross section at 1042$\,$nm to be $σ^{\,\bigstar}_{1042}=(0.89\pm0.14)\cdot 10^{-21}\,\text{m}^2$ or $σ^{\,\blacktriangle}_{1042}=(2.9\pm0.5)\cdot 10^{-21}\,\text{m}^2$. depending on the employed 532$\,$nm NV$^-$ absorption cross section.
summary: This paper characterizes the nitrogen-vacancy center's singlet transition and its phonon sideband using advanced absorption spectroscopy at room temperature. By employing cavity enhancement and novel microwave-induced signal analysis, the authors quantify the fundamental absorption cross sections of these transitions. This work significantly advances the feasibility and sensitivity of NV-based magnetometers for practical applications.
main_problem: The goal is to develop highly sensitive, room-temperature magnetometry using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond by characterizing the magnetic-field-dependent absorption properties of the NV singlet transition and its phonon sideband.
main_result: The study successfully quantifies the room-temperature absorption cross sections for the singlet transition ($\sigma^{\star}_{1042} \approx 0.89 \cdot 10^{-21} 	ext{ m}^2$) using novel cavity-enhanced and microwave-induced techniques.
method: The research combines cavity-enhanced spectroscopy, which measures signal changes under pump and microwave fields, with detailed rate model calculations to isolate the intrinsic absorption cross section from background effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is NV centers in diamond. The analysis involves modeling the electronic state evolution using a density matrix approach governed by coupled differential equations, alongside experimental measurements utilizing high-finesse optical cavities and microwave excitation.
key_observables: Absorption cross sections ($\sigma$), Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) contrast ($C_{	ext{QSP}}$), and cavity signal changes ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation, spectral range of 680-1050 nm, specific absorption wavelengths like 1042 nm, and Rabi frequencies ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The use of normalization techniques is employed to eliminate the cavity enhancement effect; a novel method using microwave-induced changes is used to suppress contributions from other defects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the NV energy level diagram and experimental setup. Key figures show cavity resonances under different excitation conditions (Bare, Pump, MW) and plot calculated signal changes ($\alpha$) versus pump power, demonstrating transitions between amplification and absorption regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the promise of absorption-based magnetometry over fluorescence methods to detailing the experimental setup using cavity enhancement. It then presents advanced analysis involving rate modeling (density matrix) to derive quantitative cross sections for the singlet transition across its phonon sideband, validating results through multiple measurement techniques.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum sensing by providing precise spectroscopic characterization of solid-state qubits (NV centers) under ambient conditions. The combination of cavity QED principles with detailed rate modeling offers a robust framework for understanding open quantum systems in materials science.
